chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to visit us. Um Ayman had gifted us milk, butter, and dates, so we presented some of it to him. He ate, then stood up to a corner of the house and prayed two rak'ahs. When he was in the final prostration, he cried a severe cry. None of us asked him out of reverence and awe for him. Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came and sat in his lap and said: 'O Father, you entered our house and we were not pleased by anything as pleased as by your entry. Then you cried a cry that grieved us; what made you cry?' He said: 'O my son, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to me just now and informed me that you will be killed and your places of martyrdom will be scattered.' He said: 'O Father, what is [the reward] for those who visit our graves while they are scattered?' He said: 'O my son, those are groups from my nation who visit you and seek blessings thereby. It is incumbent upon me to visit them on the Day of Resurrection until I deliver them from the terrors of the Hour and from their sins, and Allah will make them dwell in Paradise.'

key_terms.أَهْوَال السَّاعَة: Terrors of the Hour (Day of Judgment)
key_terms.أُمُّ أَيْمَنَ: Um Ayman, the nursemaid of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the scattered graves of the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s deep emotional connection to the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating how the revelation of future martyrdoms serves as a spiritual catalyst for the practice of Ziyarah. It establishes a unique eschatological promise where the Prophet personally intervenes to cleanse the sins of visitors and deliver them from the terrors of the Hour, reinforcing the intercessory role of the Imams within Shia theology.
